text:
sarah: heads up — saw a regression on host-side p99 for short requests after the kernel selector change. p99 for 1-8 token requests jumped ~2.3x on the egress path :thinking:

mike: timeline? did this land with the kernel affinity heuristic last night?

sarah: yeah merged ~1740 UTC. regression only when kv-cache hit rate < 30% and batch size < 4. looks like selector is picking the wide-kernel path which increases context copy cost for tiny payloads.

devon: can you paste the perf snippet? curious where the cycles go.

sarah: pasted a trimmed sample from perf-top: 
```
Samples: 1000 of event 'cycles'
  38%  host-runtime: memcpy_small
  22%  host-runtime: grpc_frame_unpack
  15%  host-runtime: tokenizer_split
  10%  host-runtime: kv_cache_eviction
   8%  kernel: wide_attention_dispatch
   7%  other
```

alyssa: interesting that memcpy_small dominates — could be repeated allocations in proto unpack path. did the grpc framing change to use smaller fragments?

mike: i changed fragmenter to prefer 512B frames for low-latency but that increases syscall churn. maybe writev coalescing got disabled for tiny frames.

tj: i ran a microbench: grpc writev throughput with 64B chunks vs 512B chunks: tail-latency for 64B is ~4.8ms vs 1.1ms for 512B (same RPS). suspect more syscalls + scheduler latency.

devon: kv thrash shows up too — when cache hit rate low we fallthrough to model and then the wide kernel does a larger KV prefetch/serialize cycle which does a few extra memmoves. combined cost = bad.

sarah: agreed. quick triage plan: 1) revert fragmenter heuristic for tiny requests OR re-enable coalescing for host-proxy; 2) force narrow-kernel for requests < 16 tokens when kvcache hit < 50% as a temporary fallback; 3) add tracing span for memcpy_small to confirm allocation sites.

alyssa: +1. for (1) i can try toggling writev batching in proxy for a canary. how do we flip it at runtime?

mike: proxy has a runtime flag `--egress-coalesce-ms` and `--min-coalesce-bytes`. set to 2ms and 256 bytes should re-coalesce without full deploy.

sarah: thanks. i'll patch selector:
```
if (tokens <= 16 && kv_hit_rate < 0.5) {
  kernel_hint = NARROW_FAST_PATH;
}
```

tj: can you also capture a full flamegraph for the mini workload? i want to compare samples before/after. use `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` on the canary host and upload.

devon: FYI ingest-bot posted a recent deploy: "deploy-service: host-runtime v3.12.1 -> v3.13.0" at 1742 UTC.

ingest-bot: deploy-service: host-runtime v3.12.1 -> v3.13.0 (canary: 3 hosts) :rocket:

mike: flipping `--min-coalesce-bytes` on canary now (set 256). canary telemetry should show p50/p99 in ~2 mins.

sarah: running a quick A/B with narrow-kernel patch on a single canary host. will post flamegraphs and tail numbers. :hammer:

alyssa: if that reduces memcpy hotspots we should consider a longer-term fix: move small-fragment parsing to a pooled buffer arena to avoid repeated allocations.

tj: also add metric: `host.rpc.coalesce.effective_bytes` so we can see how often coalescing actually triggers. right now it's opaque.

mike: acked. creating PR to add metric and the runtime flag docs.

sarah: update — after enabling coalesce and forcing narrow-kernel for tiny requests: p99 for 1-8 tokens dropped from 18.2ms -> 7.6ms on canary, payloads per-second unchanged. memcpy_small down to 14% of cycles in perf sample.

devon: nice! can we run longer soak to make sure kv miss path doesn't reintroduce tail?

sarah: running 30m soak now. if green we'll ship kernel hint as a safe fallback and open a follow-up to optimize allocator and proto-unpack.

alyssa: documented the follow-up: "preallocated arenas for proto/unpack + coalesce telemetry". leaving a note for product teams — small request SLAs improved but we're toggling fragmenter.
